speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bouts of bronchitis; to better understand your condition, how long have you had these symptoms, and do they occur seasonally or year-round?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports a chronic cough with copious, thick, yellow-green, foamy sputum for 11 years, worse in the mornings, despite being a non-smoker. Given the long duration and the specific "foamy" description, have you had any history of nasal congestion, post-nasal drip, or heartburn/acid reflux?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchiitis.

Given your 11-year history of chronic productive cough, recurrent exacerbations requiring antibiotics, and the absence of smoking, the clinical definition of chronic bronchitis (cough and sputum production for at least three months in each of two consecutive years) is met.
